summary: Non-deterministic embedding ordering from batched client requests causing rerank quality regressions and intermittent timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent degradation in rerank quality after migrating to batched embedding upload. The reranker returns different top-k ordering for identical input when embeddings are sent as a single batched payload vs. multiple single-item requests. In some high-throughput cases the rerank endpoint also returns 504 timeouts.

Impact:
- Production search relevance for LumenDocs users degraded (reported flipped top-3 results).
- Automated QA detected a 6-10% drop in NDCG for a canonical prompt set when using batched uploads.
- Occasional 504s during peak ingestion windows impacting throughput.

Environment:
- Customer on Dedicated plan, prod-us-east cluster.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On client, assemble embedding batch of 16 documents and POST to /v1/embeddings with content-type application/json and no ordering header.
2) Immediately call /v1/rerank with ranking request referencing the same document ids in the original order.
3) Compare returned top-k to results from sending 16 separate embedding calls (single-document per request) followed by rerank.
4) Repeat under load (10 concurrent clients) to observe intermittent 504s on rerank.
logs: 2026-03-09T14:12:03Z - embedding-upload - req_id=abc123 - batch_size=16 - header X-Embedding-Order: MISSING
observed_behavior: Rerank returns a consistently different ordering for a subset of batched uploads compared to single-upload baseline. Under concurrent load the rerank endpoint occasionally times out (504) with backend logs showing rebatching and KV cache misses.
expected_behavior: Embedding order should be preserved end-to-end by default. Reranker should return stable top-k equivalence for identical vectors regardless of client batching, and timeouts should not increase when using batching within configured limits.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Marta Rodriguez (Support): Customer provided example dataset and request traces. Requested priority escalation.
2026-03-10 - Evan Chen (SRE): Reproduced locally using customer dataset. Observed server-side index permutation when no ordering header present.
2026-03-11 - LumenDocs (Customer): Provided additional logs and said change coincided with SDK 2.1.0 rollout.
2026-03-11 - Rebecca Lin (Eng): Hypothesis: batch-reorder middleware introduced to optimize packing is dropping deterministic order metadata under certain header combinations.
2026-03-12 - Evan Chen (SRE): Deployed a canary fix to serving-runtime on a subset of customer nodes to preserve order; monitoring NDCG metric and 504 rate.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: embedding vector dimension mismatch or normalization changed - ruled out by checksum of vectors between single vs batched uploads (vectors identical but order permuted).
Reproducer: running curl-based sequence showed permuted ordering only when Content-Length chunking was present and X-Embedding-Order header absent.

Tracing shows batch dispatcher uses a deterministic packing algorithm but relies on client-supplied order header to map back to original ids. If header missing, it used worker-local queue ordering which is non-deterministic under concurrency.
504s correlated with increased rebatching when KV cache miss occurred because some workers processed permuted subsets causing extra cross-worker KV fetches.
Root cause: middleware introduced in serving-runtime v3.6.1 removes X-Embedding-Order for payloads >8KB due to an edge-case in header forwarding code path when proxy chunking is enabled.
Customer SDK 2.1.0 started sending batched payloads that trigger the >8KB path.
workarounds: 1) Client: set header 'X-Embedding-Order' with a comma-separated index list when sending batched embeddings.
2) Short-term: reduce embedding batch size to <=8 to avoid proxy chunking path.
3) If using SDK v2.1.0, temporarily pin to v2.0.x until server fix is rolled out.
4) For critical rerank endpoints, enable dedicated routing to a stable worker pool via the customer's dedicated config.
resolution: Canary patch applied to serving-runtime (fix PR github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123) restores header forwarding for chunked payloads and forces a deterministic mapping when header is absent. Patch rolled to 20% of customer nodes on prod-us-east on 2026-03-12. Initial telemetry shows top-k NDCG returned to baseline for canary customers and 504 rate reduced by ~78% for LumenDocs on canary nodes. Full rollout scheduled after 48h monitoring.
next_steps: 1) Complete full rollout to prod-us-east cluster after 48h of canary monitoring (owner: Evan Chen).
2) Add end-to-end integration test that validates embedding ordering equivalence for batched vs single uploads in CI (owner: Rebecca Lin).
3) Update SDK docs and add a client-side warning in SDK v2.1.x to set X-Embedding-Order for large batches until fix is fully rolled out (owner: SDK team).
4) Postmortem and add runbook entry for embedding-order issues and monitoring alert for sudden NDCG regressions (owner: Support).
